questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were multiple aspects including choosing an ambitious and good university and experiencing a new country and having the opportunity to travel a lot.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The host university was not that good at providing specifically law students the right information on study units and how we were supposed to choose and submit these in time. The proces was overwhelming and not very well guided.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a study counselor from the host university who was supposed to help the exchange students with questions and in choosing study units. This was in theory good, but there was limited help from the counselor who had maybe 100 other students to attend to at the same time.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of options in Sydney for finding apartments or rooms to rent. My roommate and I were on several rent websites were you can create a profile. We found our appartement after two weeks of staying in an airbnb. I would highly recommend that one first start looking for appartements after arrival, because most landlords require in person inspection.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Sydney is a big city so student should try to prioritize housing in suburbs closer to campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The university sent detailed emails out to students with guides on registration.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The student counselor via mail or the universities website.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very successful. Speaking from a law point of view, it was impossible to get all the classes I originally had submitted because they were all full or did not fit into the timetable. There was not a lot of guidance and it was stressfull trying to make the timetable fit for all the classes. I ended up with 2/4 classes that I had originally wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would advise future exchange students to ask for prior approval on as many subjects as possible so the timetable process won't become as stressful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The MA courses were of a high level and were manageable but challenging for someone studying a master in law at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There is mandatory in class teaching and sometimes also mandatory participation that makes out some of your final grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Copyright and Designs
War Law
Conflict of Laws
Private International Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend taking as many of the elective courses as possible rather than the mandatory courses. I would recommend war law and private international law because of the not so difficult material and easy exam forms.

questions.answer: X

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Enjoy the city and visit some of the many beaches

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. The language is English and the culture is similar to danish

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not any cultural differences but it was challenging at times that Australia is so far away from home

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The easy way of living that is more laid back and outdoorsy

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
The courses are quite challenging so you will still have to study a lot, but remember to also enjoy free time and travel!
Research and be prepared to have many different course options
Try to interact with some australian students in each of your classes, it can be a big help :)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many new friends and getting to travel around in Australia

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing study and freetime
